findings.text: The manifest declares status: complete while its after_suite object reads exit_status 'pending', completed false and log_path 'suite-after.log', no failure_count, and that path does not exist in the run directory; its baseline_suite failure_ids is ['probe'], a string naming no collected test, where suite-baseline.log ends '7 failed, 91 passed' with seven FAILED node ids; its tests line says 'pending until the two arms complete'; and outside_scope is 'pending' although the WEST arms are unmeasured. A promotion reading this manifest cannot fill a gate receipt or read the suite delta, so the run's own evidence is unreadable as delivered.

The arm recorded at the reviewed head 9d4075126 (3 677 bytes) was killed mid-run: it carries per-test output but no pytest summary line and no EXIT=, so it is not a readable arm. The only complete after arm is after-suite-37ac50088.log at 37ac50088; the two commits to head change only the fragment and the bound test's docstring, so the result transfers, but the manifest names a head arm it does not hold.

The rebaselined entry names revision 424ec19588df6fffb41e454f70eb2b2720976780 and a rewritten operator, but this file is outside the node's declared write paths. The lead's 2026-11-19 ruling (resume-3 advice, item 3) authorises re-baselining the pin, so the change itself is in scope; the dispatch declaration and manifest's changed_paths are what fail to name the path, leaving the diff's one out-of-declaration file unexplained.

extreme()'s dense branch rebuilds the metric, forms metric @ operator / mu0 and solves the generalised symmetric eigenproblem, which is exactly the linear-basis path of nova/biot/magnetisation.py:338 galerkin_spectrum; it neither calls nor extends that owner. The Lanczos branch below is new capability, but the dense branch duplicates the owner and can drift from it, and every shell row in the fragment that used this script reports a quotient computed twice.

volume_mutual() repeats the section-quadrature volume block already written at scripts/iron_operator_bound/localise.py:108 and in the owner at nova/biot/tiledassembly.py:2370-2385 (batch section_nodes, one _polygon_current_response, weighted rows); the criterion this run chose was read from the copy, so a change to the owner's batching or weighting leaves the measurement describing a block the assembler no longer builds.

gate_shell() is copied verbatim into compare.py:41, localise.py:48, nearfield.py:36, shells.py:48 and selfcell.py, one literal per module; the repository has no owner for the closed octagonal shell, so this is internal duplication rather than a fork of an owner, but five copies of the gate geometry are five places a mesh change must be repeated.

The new columns parameter (a boolean mask over source polygons, line 2122) is rebound inside the tile loop as the per-tile column-index array, so one name carries the caller's mask and the loop's index vector in the same function; a later reader following columns from the signature finds the mask consumed at line 2148 and then a different value at 2161-2162.
